scenes.title: Achilles Cannot Sleep
scenes.summary: The gathering breaks up and the army turns to supper and sleep, but Achilles weeps for Patroclus, tossing this way and that and wandering on the shore. At each dawn he ties Hector behind his chariot and drags him three times around the mound of Patroclus, then leaves him face down in the dust; Apollo keeps all defilement from the body and covers it with the golden aegis.

scenes.title: The Gods Pity Hector
scenes.summary: The blessed gods look on with pity and urge Hermes to steal the body. All but Hera, Poseidon and Athena agree; they keep the hatred they first conceived for Ilios because of Alexander, who insulted the goddesses when they came to his farmyard and praised the one who gave him grievous lust.

scenes.title: Apollo's Protest and the Will of Zeus
scenes.summary: On the twelfth dawn Apollo reproaches the gods: they will not save Hector, who burned them offerings, but favor Achilles, a man without pity or shame. Hera answers that Hector and Achilles cannot have equal honor, since Achilles is a goddess' son, and all the gods came to the wedding of Peleus. Zeus rules that Hector will not be stolen, but that Thetis shall bid Achilles accept gifts from Priam and release the body.

scenes.title: Iris Summons Thetis
scenes.summary: Iris plunges into the sea between Samos and Imbros and finds Thetis in a cave among the sea goddesses, weeping for her son's fate. Veiled in black, Thetis goes up to Olympus, where Hera gives her a golden cup, and Zeus tells her of the nine days' quarrel among the gods and charges her to tell Achilles that the gods are angry, while he sends Iris to Priam.

scenes.title: Thetis and Achilles
scenes.summary: Thetis finds Achilles groaning in his hut while his companions prepare a meal. She bids him eat and sleep, since his own death is near, and tells him that Zeus is angry and that he must accept a ransom for the body. Achilles consents: let him who brings the ransom take the body away.

scenes.title: Iris Comes to Priam
scenes.summary: Zeus sends Iris to Priam with the message: he is to go alone to the ships, with one older herald to drive the wagon, and take gifts to Achilles; Hermes will lead him, and Achilles will not kill him. Iris finds Priam in his courtyard, his head and neck covered with dung, his sons weeping around him and his daughters lamenting through the house.

scenes.title: Priam and Hecuba
scenes.summary: Priam has his sons make ready the mule wagon and tells Hecuba of the message. She cries out against his going to the man who killed so many of his sons, and wishes she could eat Achilles' liver. Priam refuses to be held back, since he has seen and heard the goddess himself, and takes from his chests the ransom: robes, cloaks, rugs, mantles, tunics, ten talents of gold, two tripods, four cauldrons and a Thracian cup.

scenes.title: Priam Drives Out the Trojans and Rebukes His Sons
scenes.summary: Priam drives the Trojans from the colonnade with his staff and abuses his nine surviving sons as liars and dancers, wishing they had died in Hector's place. They bring out the mule wagon, lash the yoke to the pole, load the ransom and yoke the mules that the Mysians gave Priam, and the horses he kept for himself.

scenes.title: The Libation and the Eagle
scenes.summary: Hecuba brings wine in a golden cup and bids Priam pour a libation and pray for a bird of omen on the right. He washes his hands, prays to Zeus of Ida to let him come to Achilles welcomed and pitied, and Zeus sends an eagle, the dark hunter, with wings as wide as a rich man's door, darting on the right across the city.

scenes.title: Zeus Sends Hermes
scenes.summary: Priam drives out of the city with the herald Idaeus in the wagon before him, and his family follows him to the plain lamenting, as if he were going to his death. Zeus pities him and sends Hermes to bring him unseen to Achilles; Hermes binds on his golden sandals, takes his wand, and goes in the likeness of a young prince.

scenes.title: Hermes Guides Priam
scenes.summary: At nightfall, as the mules and horses drink at the river beyond the mound of Ilus, Idaeus sees a man coming. Hermes takes Priam's hand, calls himself an attendant of Achilles, a Myrmidon, and tells him that Hector's body lies unharmed, fresh as dew, its wounds closed, because the gods care for him. Refusing Priam's cup, he drives the chariot to the ships, puts the sentries to sleep, opens the gate of Achilles' courtyard, reveals himself, and returns to Olympus.

scenes.title: Priam Supplicates Achilles
scenes.summary: Priam goes in unseen, clasps Achilles' knees and kisses his man-slaying hands, and Achilles marvels. Priam bids him remember his own father, tells of his fifty sons and Hector, and asks pity for one who has kissed the hand of his son's killer. Both weep, Priam for Hector and Achilles for his father and for Patroclus; then Achilles raises him and speaks of the two jars of Zeus, of Peleus' good fortune and his one doomed son, and of Priam's lost prosperity.

scenes.title: The Ransom Is Taken
scenes.summary: Priam refuses to sit while Hector lies uncared for; Achilles warns him not to stir his anger. With Automedon and Alcimus he goes out, unyokes the animals, brings in the herald, and takes the ransom, leaving two mantles and a tunic for the body. He has the slave women wash and anoint Hector out of Priam's sight, lifts him onto a bier himself, and asks Patroclus not to be angry, promising him a share of the ransom.

scenes.title: Niobe, the Meal and the Truce
scenes.summary: Achilles tells Priam that his son is released and bids him eat, as Niobe ate after Apollo and Artemis killed her twelve children. They eat, and then gaze at each other in wonder. Priam asks for sleep, and beds are made in the porch; Achilles asks how many days the funeral will take, and grants a truce of eleven days, taking the old man's right hand by the wrist.

scenes.title: Hermes Brings Priam Home
scenes.summary: While gods and men sleep, Hermes wakes Priam and warns him of the ransom his sons would have to pay if Agamemnon found him. He yokes the horses and mules and drives them unseen through the camp to the ford of the Xanthus, where he leaves them as Dawn spreads over the earth.

scenes.title: Troy Receives Hector
scenes.summary: Cassandra, looking out from Pergamus, sees her father and the body and cries out to the city, and every man and woman goes to meet them at the gates. Andromache and Hecuba tear their hair over Hector; Priam bids the crowd make way, and in the house Hector is laid on a corded bed with singers to lead the dirge.

scenes.title: Andromache's Lament
scenes.summary: Andromache, holding Hector's head, laments that he died young and left her a widow and their son an infant; the city will fall without its guardian, and she and the boy will be slaves, unless some Achaean hurls him from the tower; Hector did not die in his bed and leave her a last word.

scenes.title: Hecuba's Lament
scenes.summary: Hecuba mourns the son dearest to the gods: Achilles sold her other sons across the sea, but dragged Hector around the mound of Patroclus, and still he lies fresh as dew, like one killed by Apollo's gentle arrows.

scenes.title: Helen's Lament
scenes.summary: Helen mourns the dearest of her husband's brothers: in twenty years Hector never spoke an unkind word to her, and restrained others who reproached her; now no one in Troy is kind to her, and all shudder at her.

scenes.title: The Funeral of Hector
scenes.summary: Priam bids the Trojans bring wood without fear of an ambush, since Achilles has ordered that they be left unharmed until the twelfth dawn. For nine days they gather wood; on the tenth they burn Hector, and the next day they quench the pyre with wine, gather his bones into a golden chest wrapped in purple, lay it in a grave under great stones, heap up the mound with watchmen around it, and feast in Priam's house. So they buried Hector, tamer of horses.

days.label: Day 29
days.note: The games for Patroclus end: the gathering breaks up and the army goes to supper and sleep (24.1–3).

days.label: Days 30–38
days.note: Night after night Achilles cannot sleep; at each dawn he drags Hector three times around the mound of Patroclus (24.3–18), Apollo keeps the body from harm (24.18–21), and the gods look on with pity (24.22–30).

days.label: Day 39
days.note: "The twelfth dawn" (24.31), counted, as Hermes counts it, from the day Hector fell (24.413–414): Apollo protests, Thetis is summoned, and Iris brings Zeus' message to Priam, who sets out for the ships.

days.label: Night of Day 39
days.note: "Darkness had now come over the earth" when Priam reaches the river (24.351): Hermes brings him to Achilles, who releases the body and grants eleven days of truce; Hermes wakes Priam before dawn and brings him to the Xanthus.

days.label: Day 40
days.note: Dawn spreads over the earth as Priam crosses the Xanthus (24.695); Hector is brought home and mourned, and Priam sends the Trojans for wood.

days.label: Days 40–48
days.note: For nine days the Trojans gather wood (24.784).

days.label: Day 49
days.note: On the tenth dawn Hector is carried out and burned (24.785–787).

days.label: Day 50
days.note: At the next dawn the pyre is quenched, the bones gathered and buried, the mound heaped up and the funeral feast held in Priam's house (24.788–804); Achilles' truce runs to the twelfth day (24.667, 24.781).
